content: 1. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of voriconazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapy. 3. Voriconazole elevates the levels and effects of riociguat through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If used, monitor for hypotension and adjust the riociguat dose as needed. 4. Ritonavir increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. 5. Voriconazole increases the systemic concentration and effect of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Concurrent use may lead to increased romidepsin levels and QTc prolongation. 6. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered, reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID for patients with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use in patients with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 7. Voriconazole decreases the efficacy of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative therapy. Systemic or oral antifungals may reduce probiotic activity. 8. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose as per its prescribing information. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the original selumetinib dose. 10. Both sevoflurane and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered, consider reducing the simvastatin dose to minimize the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 13. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of siponimod by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of siponimod with drugs causing moderate CYP2C9 inhibition and moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibition is not recommended. 14. Both siponimod and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Both solifenacin and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Both sotalol and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Voriconazole and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 20. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Both sunitinib and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Both tacrolimus and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Both tetrabenazine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Tipranavir also increases voriconazole levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily. 29. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 31. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Tucatinib increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as per product labeling. 33. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Voriconazole increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 35. Both vandetanib and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Voriconazole also increases vandetanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 36. Both vemurafenib and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of vemurafenib with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. Voriconazole may also increase vemurafenib levels. 37. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Voriconazole increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 39. Voriconazole increases the toxicity of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%; reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 40. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the pre-inhibition dose. 42. Both albuterol and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Dose reduction of alfentanil may be warranted. 44. Both alfuzosin and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Alpelisib decreases voriconazole levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 50. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Both amoxapine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Apalutamide decreases voriconazole levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if coadministration is necessary. 53. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Both apomorphine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Both arformoterol and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Both artemether/lumefantrine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Voriconazole also increases the plasma concentration and effect of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 60. Both atomoxetine and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of avatrombopag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. When treating ITP, coadministration with moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors requires a reduced avatrombopag starting dose. Refer to the drug monograph for specific recommendations. 63. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Both bedaquiline and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 65. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 66. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Bosentan decreases voriconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 69. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. 70. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 71. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration and effect of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, monitor the patient for withdrawal symptoms.
